focus: Source/test review of StudioPalette production background pairings, alpha compositing, >=4.5:1 text and >=3:1 essential state-cue assertions. Footer and geometry checks excluded.

inspected.inspection: Relevant palette, background and layering call sites inspected

checks.result: m02-m03-code-v2 explicitly requires app-controlled action/secondary text >=4.5:1 on declared light/dark backgrounds and essential non-text state/control cues >=3:1; runtime acceptance remains required.

All tested palette colors are taken directly from StudioPalette production UIColors; adaptive dark/light action, secondary, warning/selection, destructive and prominent foreground values are not duplicated by the tests.

The tests resolve systemBackground, systemGroupedBackground, secondarySystemGroupedBackground and tertiarySystemGroupedBackground for light/dark with base/elevated traits. Source review confirms grouped cards/rows and explicit project-name disabled fill use the declared surfaces.

The test resolves opaque source RGBA to standard sRGB, validates finite bounded components and opacity, then composes 12% selection tint over the secondary grouped card and nested 13% icon tint over selected/unselected rows. The inspected StudioView and NeutralCardInspector call sites use those factors and layering.

StudioPlanMarkers uses selected 25% marker-color fill and unselected 65% black fill. Tests compose these over the production fixed Plan background, enforce >=3:1 for icons and light outline, >=4.5:1 for white Plan title, and separately assert fixed Plan colors do not vary by appearance.

The matrix asserts >=4.5:1 for action, secondary, warning and error text. Project checks assert >=3:1 for current-project checkmark and archived-project trash icon, >=4.5:1 for prominent foreground/action fill and secondary foreground/disabled tertiary grouped fill; relevant ProjectLibraryView call sites match.

The helper performs sRGB linearization with the 0.04045 breakpoint, standard relative luminance weighting and (lighter+0.05)/(darker+0.05), logging named pairs and resolved RGB values before threshold assertions. No fallback component value or duplicated palette swatch can silently substitute for failed UIKit resolution.

limitations: Remote source inspection only; no host, Apple toolchain, simulator, UIKit runtime, app screenshot, or native test execution was available. No numerical runtime ratio or test pass is claimed.
Startup scripts agent_cycle.py check/next, worktree status and local branch inspection could not run; the assignment was anchored to the supplied immutable GitHub commit.
Production call-site review was limited to the listed palette/background consumers; this is not an exhaustive rendered UI audit, platform accessibility audit or review of all app surfaces.
Footer and geometry checks were deliberately outside the assigned scope.

Several guessed optional source filenames returned 404 and GitHub default-branch symbol search returned no matches; the relevant actual files were then retrieved directly at the supplied commit and are listed above.
conclusion: No concrete must-fix issue found in the inspected palette definitions, compositing model, production pairings or contrast assertion thresholds. Native execution and recorded observed ratios remain required for acceptance.
